column4: Visit note | 2025-10-06 10:00 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Shirin Patwary, 27, female. Mrs. Patwary returns for a follow-up review regarding irregular periods, extra hair on the face, and acne. She mentions that she noticed weight gain after starting a desk job in Tangail. She is a mobile phone repair technician. She has a known comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. She denies severe pelvic pain or unexpected bleeding changes. On examination: BMI 25.7, BP 130/86 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 73 kg. Abdomen is soft and non-tender. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: continue current medicines, no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-10-06 11:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Mahiya Dewan, 26, female. Ms. Dewan comes in because she is bothered by acne and irregular periods. She explains that she noticed weight gain after starting a desk job in Old Dhaka. She works as a fisherman. She reports no other major medical conditions. She denies recent vision changes or severe headaches. On examination: BMI 31.6, BP 119/78 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 86 kg. Skin shows facial blemishes and some hirsutism. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-10-07 03:00 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Tamim Rahman, 79, male. Mr. Rahman reports burning in both feet, numbness in the toes, and symptoms worse at night. He states this was noticed after long hours standing at a factory in Barishal. He works as a shopkeeper. He reports no associated chronic illnesses. He denies any recent falls or open skin lesions on his legs. On examination: reduced sensation at 6 of 10 monofilament test sites, BP 116/80 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, weight 43 kg. Deep tendon reflexes are sluggish at the ankles. Assessment: Peripheral neuropathy. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment, including HbA1c, vitamin B12, and a nerve conduction study; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. He was advised to check the feet daily for cuts, wear soft closed shoes, and keep blood sugar under control. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-10-09 02:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Rashid Awal, 31, male. Mr. Awal describes experiencing neck tightness, stress, and long hours at a screen. He mentions his trouble started during a deadline month at an office in Rampura. He works as a photographer. He has no prior medical history of note. He denies visual disturbances, fever, or limb weakness. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 117/83 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 85 kg. Neck muscles are tender to palpation with normal range of motion. Assessment: Tension-type headache. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. He was advised to take screen breaks every hour, do neck stretches, and sleep seven hours. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-10-13 11:30 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Nargis Sultana, 48, female. Mrs. Sultana explains that light hurting the eyes and a throbbing headache on one side have been troubling her. She reports her condition has been worse since bright screens at a new job in Rampura. She works as a bus driver. She has no other chronic health conditions. She denies any history of head injury or sudden neurological deficits. On examination: about 13 headache days a month, BP 123/78 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 84 kg. Cranial nerves are intact. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up after the test results are ready.

Visit note | 2025-10-14 10:00 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Jubayer Akand, 59, male. Mr. Akand reports itchy dry patches on the elbows and knees and symptoms worse in winter. He notes his condition flared during the dry winter in Gulshan. He works as a lawyer. He denies any significant past medical illnesses. He denies oozing or signs of secondary skin infection. On examination: affected area about 11 cm across, BP 124/73 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 77 kg. Skin shows erythematous plaques with scaling over the extensor surfaces. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: tests ordered before starting treatment: no tests; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up after the test results are ready.
